editorial:
Imagine the biggest star in the country suddenly turning up dead, and practically everyone in the industry had a reason to do it. That is the wild setup you get here. You are dropped right into the chaotic world of Japanese show business, where the victim, Wada Akiko, was basically the boss of everyone. From the fancy managers to the stressed-out TV staff and even random pachinko workers, there are over a thousand people who could be the killer. The vibe is a mix of a serious crime investigation and a peek behind the curtain of fame, showing you how messy and mean the entertainment world can actually be when the cameras stop rolling.

What really makes this work is how it keeps you guessing with a huge list of suspects. The acting feels grounded, making the tension feel real as the mystery unfolds. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the payoff is totally worth it. If you enjoy stories where you can play detective, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend if you want something that keeps your brain working.
endingExplained: The mystery wraps up by revealing that the murder was not committed by a high-profile rival, but someone closer to the inner circle. After sorting through a mountain of lies and fake alibis, the detective proves that a person driven by deep resentment and personal betrayal pulled the trigger. The final scenes show the killer breaking down as their plan falls apart, proving that fame and power often create the most dangerous enemies in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic whodunit mysteries and celebrity drama.
